claim: Lunapark has intrinsic ubiquitin-ligase activity in its N-terminal 45 aa
finding: Lnp purified from mammalian cells shows in vitro Ub-ligase activity; activity attributed partly to associated ligase (gp78/AMFR identified by AP-MS) and partly to an intrinsic activity mapped to aa 1-45; authors state the segment has no homology to any known ligase motif
context: HEK293-type mammalian cells; AP-MS; in vitro ubiquitination of protein purified from mammalian lysate
confidence: Single source, never independently replicated in 10 years. Protein purified from mammalian cells cannot exclude sub-stoichiometric co-purifying E3. No catalytic residue identified, no point mutant that kills activity while sparing folding.

finding: Residues 1-45 contain 0 Cys and 0 His; coiled coil 16-41; N-myristoyl Gly2. All 13 reviewed lunapark orthologs have 0 Cys in aa 1-45. HECT/RBR need a catalytic Cys; RING/U-box need Zn ligands or a ~70 aa zinc-free RING fold.
context: Human Q9C0E8 plus 12 ortholog sequences from UniProt reviewed
confidence: High for the chemical argument. Does not exclude an entirely novel, non-thioester, non-RING mechanism.

claim: The C-terminal C4 zinc finger is a RING/U-box module
finding: LNPK has 4 ligands/1 tetrahedral Zn site (SG-centroid 2.09-2.28 A, pLDDT 92.3); RNF4 and c-CBL RINGs have 8 ligands/2 Zn in cross-brace; CHIP U-box is zinc-free and ~70 aa. LNPK is 0% helix vs 25%/19% for the RINGs. Backbone path around the metal: 0.90 A RMSD to TFIIS zinc ribbon vs 2.20/2.27 A to the RINGs.
context: Predicted model plus deposited crystal/NMR structures
confidence: High. Caveat: no experimental structure of LNPK exists (PDBe reports none) and no zinc has been measured on purified LNPK.

claim: The LNPK zinc finger folds like a RING
finding: LNPK 265-315 vs pdb100 gave 30 hits, all zinc-ribbon-class (RNA Pol I/II/V subunits, TMEM55B, NUP153/NUP358 ZnFs) and 0 RING/U-box/HECT/RBR. Positive control with the RNF4 RING gave 412 hits led by RNF4, RNF12, RNF165, TRAF6, RNF38, RNF8, RNF125. Hit-set overlap at PDB-entry level: LNPK vs RING = 0 shared entries; LNPK vs TFIIS zinc ribbon = 3 shared.
context: Public Foldseek webserver, pdb100 and afdb50
confidence: Medium-high. A 41-residue query gives weak E-values (best 0.98); the control establishes sensitivity, and the absence of RINGs is the informative result.

claim: Domain databases call this region a RING
finding: The only domain assignment is IPR019273 "Lunapark zinc ribbon domain" (PF10058 "ER junction formation factor lunapark, zinc ribbon finger") at 256-305. Zero RING/U-box/HECT/RBR signatures match Q9C0E8 in any member database.
confidence: High as independent corroboration; database-level evidence, not experimental.

claim: Residues 1-45 are required for junction localisation because they carry ligase activity
finding: Mutating the N-myristoylation site or hydrophobic CC1 residues in the Lnp N-terminus mis-targets Lnp; purified Lnp-NT attaches to membranes in a myristoylation-dependent manner. Deleting the lunapark motif in the C-terminal zinc finger affects homo-oligomerisation but not localisation.
context: Mammalian cells, ATL-knockout lines, in vitro liposome assays
confidence: High. Provides a membrane-anchoring explanation for the 1-45 requirement that does not invoke ubiquitin ligation.

finding: CAND1, a regulator of SCF/cullin-RING ligases, binds Lnp and reduces Lnp auto-ubiquitination; CAND1 knockdown enhances proteasomal degradation of Lnp.
context: Mammalian cells, affinity chromatography, in vitro
confidence: Medium. Consistent with a cullin-RING ligase acting on Lnp rather than Lnp acting as the ligase, but the paper itself asserts an N-terminal ligase domain.

stance: refutes ligase role by role reversal
claim: Lunapark is the ligase in its ubiquitin relationship
finding: Lunapark is a substrate ubiquitylated by the CRL3-KLHL12 ubiquitin ligase at membranes; blocking Lunapark ubiquitylation causes neurodevelopmental defects.
context: Proteomic screen of membrane ubiquitylation; human cells; zebrafish development
confidence: High for substrate role. Does not formally exclude an additional ligase role.

claim: LNPK sits in a curated ubiquitin-machinery interaction network
finding: 33 curated partners for Q9C0E8, none in the ubiquitin system; gp78/AMFR, KLHL12 and CUL3 are not present.
confidence: Medium. Absence reflects curation coverage, not necessarily biology.

claim: LNPK core function is ER three-way junction stabilisation
finding: mLnp1 stabilises nascent three-way ER junctions; homozygous LNPK loss-of-function causes a recessive neurodevelopmental syndrome with aberrant ER structure and corpus callosum hypoplasia.
context: Live-cell imaging in mammalian cells; two consanguineous human families
